questions.question: Please define audience source/methodology. If you build proprietary audiences, please include sources and seeds.
questions.approved_answer: PulsePoint builds proprietary audiences using a combination of first-party HCP data, de-identified medical and pharmacy claims, and real-time behavioral and contextual signals. PulsePoint's HCP data is built on Medscape first party data. We rely on Medscape CRM as the source because re-identification requires a consented foundation-- something only Medscape provides at scale. DTC audiences are derived from millions of annual claims and enriched with engagement and content consumption signals using our patented contextual engine mapped to National Library of Medicine's taxonomy. All data is HIPAA- and NAI-compliant and refreshed continuously to maintain accuracy.

questions.question: How do you ensure compliance with global data privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, LGPD) and state health data regulations
questions.approved_answer: PulsePoint ensures compliance by using only de-identified data for DTC targeting and obtaining named, first-party consent for HCP data. We follow HIPAA, NAI, GDPR, CCPA, and LGPD guidelines, and apply Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods to protect patient privacy. Data use is governed by strict contracts, population thresholds, and internal audits to meet both global and state-level health data requirements.
questions.note: GDPR/CCPA/state health-data compliance is the legal/privacy row. Library holds an answer; the skill says not to use it.

questions.question: What identity graphs are integrated with your platform? (LiveRamp, Axciom, etc.)
questions.approved_answer: PulsePoint operates its own identity graph. We also are integrated with enternal partners such as LiveRamp/RampID and other privacy-compliant ID solutions, including UID2 and ID5.

PulsePoint builds proprietary audiences using a combination of first-party HCP data, de-identified medical and pharmacy claims, and real-time behavioral and contextual signals. === /mnt/memory/rfi-answer-library/client-strategy/loopio-11344753.md
id: loopio-11344753
question: What is the methodology behind your segment creation? (Ex. Use a seed audience that is then modeled out for distribution)
stack: Client Strategy
updated: 2024-10-14T20:03:12+00:00
tags: 
source: loopio

PulsePoint leverages a first party data foundation at the core of our business. The HCP identity graph uses the power of Medscape's physician member database to authenticate 3.2 million NPI numbers across the United States to inform and validate all HCP targeting from platform. The offline NPI numbers are translated into online IDs within a proprietary identity infrastructure and through the use of 4x verified onboarders, and campaigns are then able to reach the physicians within their digital footprint. PulsePoint is specifically focused to developing a best-in-class, accurate translation of the NPI number to digital ID, which has generated an NPI graph that has an addressability rate of 90%+ on average (i.e. with 10k NPIs, PulsePoint can deliver to 9.5k of those within a 30-day window). 
 
 Customized consumer audiences are created using claims data signals such as ICD-10 codes, J-Codes, NDC Codes, and CPT codes to develop a seed that is further modeled out based on diagnosis and treatment propensity by age, gender and zip code. The models directly reference our HIPPA compliant database of 220MM+ Patients and 3BB annual pharmacy claims powered by a Forian data claims data API and are planned and activated according to NAI privacy guidelines. Additional consumer data signals that reference our proprietary HCP database in an anonymized way, such as likely patients of target HCPs, geographical relevance to practice locations of specific HCPs are also leveraged for modeling purposes. Each model is fully customized.

=== /mnt/memory/rfi-answer-library/client-strategy/loopio-11344328.md
id: loopio-11344328
question: DTC audience methodology?
stack: Client Strategy
updated: 2024-10-14T20:00:36+00:00
tags: 
source: loopio

PulsePoint's DTC audience methodology combines medically mapped contextual data, online audience behaviors, clinical data, and signals from Internet Brands' owned and operated health sites, such as WebMD. This multi-source approach enables the identification of consumer audiences based on their medical interests, behaviors, conditions, and engagement with trusted health platforms. By integrating these diverse data points, PulsePoint delivers precise, relevant messaging to target audiences, enhancing the effectiveness of direct-to-consumer (DTC) campaigns.
 
 For DTC:
 - Bespoke Audiences: Clinical signals for DTC are the results of the production of audience models that are optimized in real time toward the prevalence of diagnosis and treatment by age, gender and zip code at delivery. Custom claims-based models based on a database of 220MM+ Patients and 3BB annual pharmacy claims. Audience models created following NAI guidelines for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions.
 -- Life science companies often utilize HCP data to inform DTC audience segmentation. 
 - Health Pages: Capture the consumer & patient’s attention the exact moment intent is signaled. Target audiences consuming relevant health content.
 - Health Populations: Target audiences who have recently engaged with content for specific health conditions and treatments. Populations are built dynamically using the entire browsing profile of the individual, which allows you to capture the user regardless of the page they are on or arriving from.
 - Health Populations+: This takes our foundational Health Populations Audiences and includes their first-party signals through PulsePoint’s proprietary access to endemic website data.
 - Rx Populations: Rx Populations reaches qualified, scalable DTC audiences without sacrificing performance by combining PulsePoint’s contextually created audiences (HealthPop) with RX data to maintain quality and scale, while having a positive impact on AQ during later stage moments of the health journey.
 - OTC Populations: Audience models created following NAI guidelines for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions
 - Keywords: Real-time keyword targeting based on keywords provided by agency, brand or PulsePoint
 - Keyword Populations: Customer audiences that have recently engaged with content containing pre-specified keywords or health specific keywords provided by PulsePoint
 - IBM Watson: Leverage real-world ZIP data where conditions are likely to be impacted by external factors (eg weather)
 
 We also have more generalized targeting capabilities such as retargeting, clickers, converters, IAB, demographic (age, gender, ethnicity), geography etc.

question: Do you have proprietary audience data available? If yes, please describe the nature of the audience available
stack: Client Strategy
updated: 2024-10-14T20:03:12+00:00
tags: 
source: loopio

Yes - PulsePoint's DSP (LIFE) is the proprietary activation software of Internet Brands, and our data spine is validated using first-party signals directly from WebMD and Medscape. We also have our own proprietary cross device solution that allows us to capture an individual-level profile and identify the devices that fall within that patient or HCPs identity graph. In using our cross device graph, PP can accurately reach the target audience on their personal and household devices, including mobile, desktop, CTV, etc. PulsePoint also uses the power of Internet Brands (i.e. Medscape) first party data to fuel the inputs of validating the NPI graph and identifying the IDs associated to any given NPI number.

=== /mnt/memory/rfi-answer-library/client-strategy/loopio-11344511.md
id: loopio-11344511
question: Are you leveraging cookies to build your seed audiences (assuming no target list audiences)?
stack: Client Strategy
updated: 2024-10-14T20:00:46+00:00
tags: 
source: loopio

Yes however cookies are just one input used in the creation of seed audiences. The total list includes:
 
 First-Party Data Integration: PulsePoint leverages its robust first-party data, sourced from Medscape and WebMD, ensuring a strong foundation for targeting and analytics without relying on third-party cookies​​​​.
 
 Identity Solutions: PulsePoint integrates with multiple external ID providers, including RampID, UID2, and ID5. This approach allows for seamless identity management and targeting across platforms without dependence on cookies​​​​.
 
 Contextual Targeting: Utilizing the PulsePoint contextualizer, ads are served based on the content of the page rather than user behavior tracking. This ensures relevance and compliance with privacy standards​​.
 
 Cookieless IDs and Single Sign-On: PulsePoint has completed its single sign-on integration with Medscape, enabling the mapping of cookieless IDs to actual identities of healthcare professionals. This allows for accurate targeting and reporting at the physician level even without cookies​​.
 
 Advanced Technologies: The company uses AI and machine learning models to predict user behavior and preferences based on available data points. This strategy does not require tracking individuals across the web, thus maintaining privacy compliance​​.
